contexts.text: The reputation of power thence. Signified, Explained.
For the sake of the reputation thence...
External bonds... thus the love of reputation...
In the works no regard for reputation, etc.
Through Knowledges of truth may gain reputation, and thence honours and wealth. AC 5280:3. AC 5376:2.
Their evil report () = their blemishes and faults.
This influx manifests itself by their (solicitude about reputation after death).
Bridle cupidities in order to capture reputation.
Desire truths not for the sake of reputation and glory.
When man is affected with truth... he is at the same time affected with reputation and glory. This latter affection is inevitable (at first) and is then permitted, that it may introduce.
A great part of the learned are sensuous: the cause is that they have learned knowledges solely for the sake of reputation, that they may be promoted to honours, and thus to gain.
Fear lest they be deprived of reputation for the sake of honours and gain. AC 7437:end. DP 139:5. CL 267:3.
Persuaded that (their) doctrines are true... for the sake of reputation.
To capture the reputation of seeming to be good.
If the end is to do good for the sake of reputation...
Those who do good from Christian charity, sometimes regard the reputation thence for the sake of honours or gain. Explained.

Thou shalt not bear a report of vanity () = no listening to Falsities. To bear a report = to hear and do, thus to listen; for reputation, in the Original, is expressed by a word which means listening.
Do not fear for their reputation (there) as in this world.
Have performed uses for the sake of reputation... These (become) the most stupid.
When he fears no loss of reputation, he can speak against God, the neighbour, etc., and also act against them...
Appears externally as moral, because he loves the reputation of this...
The Lord rules them by the celebrity of their name.
It is from this implanted Knowledge (of there being a life after death) that some aspire to an immortality of fame. Explained.
These (conjugial simulations) are for the sake of reputation...
He then poured round (his books) the glory of his reputation...
The glory of reputation has induced you to confirm what you do not believe.
Not to kill means also not to inflict any deadly evil on a man's name and reputation, for with many, reputation and life go hand and hand. AE 1012:3.
(A Spirit) who was stirred up by fear of the loss of his reputation...
On a certain most famous man in Europe, Gustavus Adolphus.
On those who have captured reputation by external probity.
Occurs. AE 721:20.
That the Word will last to eternity, is signified by as thy days thy fame ().
That those who have as the end... a reputation for erudition, do not see or find anything of genuine truth in the Word. Explained.
